samples.identification: UPX-packed Rifaien self-mutation and submission utility
evidence: UPX checksum fails. Emulation recovers mapped code and E8/E9-filter restoration; stub at 0x428610 hands control to 0x401130, CRT at 0x401020, then main at 0x4013a0.

Main obtains its own path (0x4013ce), reads the complete file (0x4013da-0x401435), finds [[UNIQUE]] (0x401470-0x40149e), waits 30000ms (0x4014e1), generates a name and mutates sixteen bytes (0x4014e9-0x40155e), and writes the copy (0x40156b-0x401599).

libcurl multipart formadd calls attach that generated file under file[], a rand()%7+1 NODE value and submit=send. setopt configures URL, HTTPPOST and VERBOSE; perform at 0x401656 sends it. Success deletes the copy. Both error and success paths return to the sleep/upload loop. The response is not tasking or staged code.

Offset 0x14c8b contains a truncated native PE with CLR meta-host GUIDs and an unrolled XOR decoder. It declares an import table and resources beyond the available bytes; it is not independently loadable. Emulating only its decoder recovers Cor_Enable_Profiling. Code contains CLR COM activation and byte-array handling, but the host does not extract, map or invoke this fragment.

Inspected CRT initialization, constructor-list handling and dynamic imports. No transfer from the host to its appended PE, attacker task dispatch, credential collection, unauthorized persistence or host-file infection was found. Its self-submission function is visible in console output and uses a fixed public upload surface; this functional evidence favors a submission experiment.
samples.uncertainty: Installation context and historical server behavior are unavailable. Uploading a mutated executable is unusual; the recipient could execute submissions. No claim that this artifact is harmless in every deployment, or that an incomplete protected-code fragment is benign when restored.

url_check.result: GET redirects to HTTPS, then http://ipv4.games/claim?name=CollabVM, a 280-byte HTML claim page, not a payload. This does not reconstruct the old upload service.

samples.source_label_explanation: Continuous self-mutation, packed code, repeated executable uploads, existing Snojan-family reputation and an appended CLR protector fragment can produce malware/sandbox labels. None establishes an attack in the recovered execution path. Outer collector family names are not behavior evidence. Fetched the exact Triage overview and behavioral page: its high-score signatures are Snojan identity and an unpacked-UPX dump; lesser signatures report hostname/language queries and unsigned packing. The recovered host contains no corresponding downloader execution chain.
samples.changes: No PE-specific change: existing notable observations describe packing, self-mutation/upload markers, XOR decoding and embedded CLR identifiers without inventing activation or theft.
samples.marker_line: Rifaien uploader: self-submission only; no payload activation

evidence: All 202 bytes are five ordinary Java-properties settings. The backslash in https\:// is Java-properties escaping; it does not hide another host. Cache and ZIP locations are wrapper/dists under GRADLE_USER_HOME.

Fetched distributionUrl and followed its official Gradle/GitHub release redirect chain. The 138576146-byte ZIP SHA-256 is 10065868c78f1207afb3a92176f99a37d753a513dff453abb6b5cceda4058cda, equal to the checksum fetched from services.gradle.org.

Inspected startup shell script and included Gradle sources: WrapperExecutor loads configuration with Properties.load, Install downloads/unzips into the selected cache, and BootstrapMainStarter invokes GradleMain via URLClassLoader. GradleMain checks Java version and enters the build launcher. This is the declared wrapper purpose.
samples.uncertainty: No enclosing project or wrapper JAR supplied. A malicious build or modified wrapper could use this ordinary config. The config omits a pinned distributionSha256Sum, but omission alone establishes no malicious intent.
samples.source_label_explanation: Likely collected with a malicious repository/build or mislabeled as a component. The supplied configuration itself specifies the official tool distribution and carries no code.
samples.changes: No change; the existing notable wrapper-remote-url trait accurately describes the declaration.

samples.identification: AntV G Lite 2.7.0 graphics engine, stored with a 2.9.0 archive filename
evidence: Fetched https://registry.npmjs.org/@antv/g-lite/2.7.0 and its tarball. Compared all 322 regular archive members: no additions, removals or byte changes. Artifact identity comes from the content, not the outer filename.

Reviewed CommonJS/ESM entry paths, UMD bundled code and source-map content. Runtime initializes scene graphs, CSS typed values, camera/matrix math and renderer services. Canvas/plugin init attaches pointer/click/wheel listeners; destroy removes them. Values near listeners are CSS/numeric fields, not captured credentials.

ImagePool creates images through the configured image factory, sets anonymous cross-origin mode, assigns the caller-provided source, caches images and tiles/downsamples with canvas/createImageBitmap. HTMLRenderingPlugin sets innerHTML for caller-provided HTML shapes. These are exposed rendering features, not an undisclosed transmission path.

The three interior slice calls in the UMD bundle divide cubic Bezier coordinate arrays at (2,4),(4,6),(6,8). They do not read a binary envelope. Switch command fields dispatch SVG path instructions. Numeric tables, regex construction and Babel wrappers serve graphics/CSS parsing and transpilation.

No install lifecycle hooks, dynamic payload evaluation, child process launch, hidden credential access or fixed exfiltration destination found. Documentation URLs are comments and source references, not load-time fetches.

Fetched and reviewed all seven direct runtime dependencies at currently resolved versions plus fast-deep-equal, the only additional runtime implementation dependency of util. @antv/vendor includes vendored D3 sources: d3-fetch uses caller-provided URLs; d3-dsv builds a row converter with JSON.stringify-escaped column names. Neither runs a hidden install action or exports secrets.
samples.uncertainty: The package has version ranges and no lockfile, so current dependency resolution is not proof of any historical installation graph. D3 packages declared by vendor are shipped as reviewed lib-vendor sources; declaration-only type packages are not executable payloads. No consuming application supplied.
samples.source_label_explanation: Archive filename disagrees with its actual version; collection context or version-level reputation can mislabel unchanged upstream bytes. Large minified bundles, source maps, dynamic UI dispatch and pointer events also provide superficial malware-like signals. The precise external labeling reason is unknown.
samples.changes: Removed click-only registration from the edit-event observation, made that complete operation notable, required form-specific value evidence for its composite, and moved untyped fixed slice syntax from buffer/record to source/syntax/call. Preserved its explicit loader consumer through a metadata composite with the original exclusions. Relocated identity-function counts to file/profile/function-population and nested-plus measurements to source/syntax/operator; a numeric-only positive control proves that ast.max_concat_chain does not establish strings.
samples.marker_line: AntV G Lite: registry-identical renderer; fix input/shape traits

validation_plan: All markers, fourteen control checks and final atomscan runs completed. Final action is make validate; command output is authoritative for validation status.
